evals.name: hidden-retention-rule
evals.prompt: A cleanup job compares timestamps against 7776000000 in three places. Review it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies a shared retention-period decision, gives it a domain name with units, and places it near the owning cleanup policy.

assertions.text: Uses a name or type with clear units
Keeps the definition near its owner

evals.name: obvious-literals-stay-inline
evals.prompt: Should we replace every 0, 1, empty string, and 8px spacing value in this small component with constants?
evals.expected_output: Rejects cosmetic extraction and leaves literals whose meaning is obvious in context inline.

assertions.text: Distinguishes harmless values from hidden decisions

evals.name: review-only-hidden-concepts
evals.prompt: Audit this module for magic values and buried rules. Report only.
evals.expected_output: Reports the value or rule, locations, meaning, and narrowest replacement without editing.

assertions.text: Reports meaning and ownership, not only literal occurrences

evals.name: implement-options-object
evals.prompt: Refactor calls like sendReport(report, true, false, 3) so their intent is visible while preserving behavior.
evals.expected_output: Replaces opaque positional arguments with a narrow options shape and meaningful names, updates callers, and runs checks.

assertions.text: Uses named options instead of positional booleans and numbers

evals.name: duplication-overlap-keeps-owner
evals.prompt: The string pending-review appears in six modules as one workflow status. Should each module define its own named constant?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes both a hidden domain state and meaningful duplication, defines it once at the workflow owner, and avoids a global constants dump.

assertions.text: Defines the workflow state once rather than once per module
Places it with the domain owner
Does not create a generic global constants file
